evidence.summary: Category B sharply lowers the score. Q3 (A) vs Q4 (B) differ only in x9 and the score falls 0.4335 -> 0.0320. Q2 (also B, with very different other inputs) gives exactly 0.0320 too, so B looks like a floor or override rather than a gradual effect.
With everything else fixed, A = 0.4335, C = 0.4375, D = 0.4415. C and D give a small gain over A (ordering D > C > A). B is the exception (see the B claim).

Higher x2 lowers the score in four single-variable comparisons: 40->60 gives 0.3538 -> 0.3225 (nearly all of it past 50; 40->50 is only -0.001), 25->45 gives 0.9714 -> 0.9637, 25->26 gives 0.9740 -> 0.9735, and 25->24 gives 0.9913 -> 0.9922.
Raising x10 from a low value helps, with diminishing returns. Early series: 0/10/20/30 -> 0.8032/0.8552/0.8816/0.8831, then 40 -> 0.8820 (plateau near 30). Later series: 15 -> 0.9717 vs 25 -> 0.9820.
Above roughly 35 the effect reverses (inverted-U, best around 25-35). With x8=40: 35 -> 0.9822, 37 -> 0.9815, 40 -> 0.9714. With x8=37 and x5=350: 36 -> 0.9905, 35 -> 0.9911, 34 -> 0.9913.

Raising x8 from 40 to 50 lowers the score in two single-variable tests (0.9597 -> 0.9464 and 0.9714 -> 0.9561). Between 35 and 40 the curve is nearly flat and peaks at 37 (35: 0.9836, 36: 0.9835, 37: 0.9842, 38: 0.9832, 39: 0.9827, 40: 0.9822).
Lowering x6 from 20 to 18 raises the score by 0.0066 (0.9597 -> 0.9663). A second series agrees: 18 -> 0.9842, 19 -> 0.9833, 20 -> 0.9796. Values below 18 were not isolated.
Going from x7=2 to x7=0 with all else equal raises the score from 0.9663 to 0.9714. Based on a single comparison.
Q10 (x4=6) and Q11 (x4=5) are identical in every other input and both score 0.3538, so x4 shows no effect between 5 and 6. Other x4 values (e.g. 0 vs 6) were never isolated.
